\label{lemma-linear-series-trivial-existence}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$.
If $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^r_d$, then $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^s_d$ for
all $0 \leq s \leq r$.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a nonsingular proper curve over $k$.
Let $(\mathcal{L}, V)$ be a $\mathfrak g^1_d$ on $X$. Then the morphism
$\varphi : X \to \mathbf{P}^1_k$ associated to the pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ by the projective-space construction above
either
\begin{enumerate}
\item is nonconstant and has degree $\leq d$, or
\item factors through a closed point of $\mathbf{P}^1_k$ and in this
case $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \not = k$.
\end{enumerate}

source_identity.original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-grd-inequalities}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper curve over $k$ with
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. If $X$ has a $\mathfrak g^r_d$, then
$r \leq d$. If equality holds, then $H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = 0$, i.e.,
the genus of $X$ (Definition \ref{definition-genus}) is $0$.

A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. For a smooth proper curve, $\omega_X\simeq\Omega_{X/k}$; if $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is invertible.
